summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening dyspnea and abdominal distension. Evaluation revealed asymmetric pulmonary edema and small pleural effusions on imaging, with elevated BNP of 5,158, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to increased oral torsemide (100 mg QAM, 60 mg QPM) to manage fluid overload. His symptoms improved, and he was weaned off oxygen. Asymptomatic bacteriuria with Citrobacter koseri and Enterococcus was noted but not treated per transplant guidelines. Potassium supplementation was initiated due to hypokalemia during diuresis. He remained stable with improved respiratory status and was discharged home with follow-up plans including repeat CT chest in three months, echocardiogram in six months, and palliative care consultation for ongoing support.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
